claim: For Algorithm 2 (Naive Separation Algorithm) in Matsuno (2026), fix \(\eta=1/10\) and any stopping tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). Let \(P=\{A,B,C\}\) with \(A=(1,-50)\), \(B=(1,-5)\), \(C=(2,50)\), and initialize \(x_0=B\). Then \(0\notin \operatorname{conv}(P)\), but the algorithm never terminates: it alternately selects \(C\) and \(A\), its clipped coefficient is \(\alpha_k=9/10\) for every \(k\), and the even and odd subsequences converge to the attracting two-cycle \(x_-^*=(28/19,-50/19)\), \(x_+^*=(29/19,50/19)\) with exact two-step factor \(81/100\). Consequently, the fixed-support-face assumption used in the paper's Theorem 3.2 is not implied by Algorithm 2, and the cap \(\alpha_k\le 1-\eta\) can prevent convergence to a separating normal even when the polytope is strictly separated from the origin.
integrity: The proof uses exact rational inequalities and an invariant-region argument. The included verifier checks the rational identities and boundary inequalities; no finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The counterexample fixes \(\eta=1/10\) and the allowed initialization \(x_0=(1,-5)\); it does not classify all parameters or starts.
The result does not contradict Theorem 3.2 under its added fixed-support-face hypothesis; it proves that Algorithm 2 does not enforce that hypothesis.
title: A fixed move floor creates an attracting two-cycle in the Naive Separation Algorithm
